new_findings.title: Rekey completion is decided per removal target, so the current generation can stay wrapped to a removed device and all new secret versions use it
evidence: ensure_removal_rotations skips a removal as `completed` if any generation carries a removal_fact_hash whose fact targets the same fingerprint.
author_commit then accepts writes under doc.dek.current. Neither step checks whether the current generation's wraps include a removed member.
rotate_dek_bound wraps for every member that is active in the rotator's own document.

Scenario (concurrent or partitioned removals): admin A removes W and rotates to G_a (bound to W, excludes W, includes V). Admin B has not seen W's removal; it removes V and rotates to G_b (bound to V, excludes V, includes W). G_b has the later HLC, so the fold makes G_b current on every node.
Both removals now count as completed, so nothing rotates again. All subsequent local secret.put_version commits pass the guard under G_b.
B, before learning of W's removal, kept a live session with W and broadcast G_b's commit. Any peer unaware of the removal can also relay it.
W can therefore unwrap the current DEK and decrypt every future shared secret version indefinitely, until some later rotation.
This contradicts §4.4 ('New secret versions use the new generation') and the §13 stage-4 claim that removed members cannot decrypt new generations.
resolution_conditions: Treat rekey as incomplete whenever dek.generations[dek.current].wraps contains any fingerprint in the removed-member set. In that case rotate again, bound to the relevant removal hash.
Make author_commit refuse secret.put_version with team_rekey_pending under the same condition. Do this independently of per-target bookkeeping.

Add a test with two concurrent removals by different admins, where the later-ordered rotation includes the other removed device. Assert that after both are received an admin rotates again, local writes are refused until it does, and the final current generation has no wrap for either removed fingerprint.
Also cover a pure ordering variant: the rotation commit arrives before its removal fact.

new_findings.title: The static OpenSSL gate validates OPENSSL_DIR, but the linker can consume other variables, and nothing checks the linked result
evidence: build.rs checks only the plain OPENSSL_DIR and OPENSSL_STATIC.

openssl-sys resolves target-prefixed variables first (for example AARCH64_APPLE_DARWIN_OPENSSL_DIR or ..._OPENSSL_STATIC). It also honors OPENSSL_LIB_DIR, OPENSSL_INCLUDE_DIR and pkg-config inputs, and these take precedence over OPENSSL_DIR.

build-release.py copies os.environ and removes only OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR. An inherited OPENSSL_LIB_DIR or target-prefixed variable (for example a Homebrew environment on a runner) can link a different, possibly dynamic, OpenSSL while build.rs passes against the pinned SDK.
No step in build-release.py or either workflow runs otool -L, ldd or a symbol check to reject a dynamic libssl/libcrypto dependency or confirm the 3.5.9 version string.
docs/releasing.md states 'Bundled archives must not link to Homebrew or system OpenSSL', but the release tooling does not enforce it. The otool evidence is manual and was not supplied.
resolution_conditions: In build-release.py, scrub OPENSSL_LIB_DIR, OPENSSL_INCLUDE_DIR, OPENSSL_LIBS, the target-prefixed OPENSSL_* variants and pkg-config overrides, or set them explicitly to the SDK.
Optionally make build.rs read the same target-prefixed variables that openssl-sys reads.
After cargo build, assert that no release binary has a dynamic libssl/libcrypto dependency (otool -L on macOS, readelf/ldd on Linux), and fail packaging if one does.
Add a test that sets a conflicting OPENSSL_LIB_DIR or target-prefixed variable and expects the build to fail.

non_findings_checked: The drain deadline cannot be extended (or_insert_with). Drain is marked before refold in every fact-application path. Removal notices are still sent to the removed target by design.

store_fact, quarantine_local_fact, author_fact (local) and the removal-repair rotation all write facts or commits under the state lock. Rejected-line rewrites match exact line content and skip hashes already accepted.
Completed-rotation dedup prevents repeated rekeys on duplicate confirmations and restart. Pending repairs are rebuilt from facts.jsonl at register_env.

Production op names: secret.put_version and dek.rotate match commit.rs validators and fold handlers. removal_fact_hash is validated as 64-hex, persisted in the document, and dek.rotate commits are never compacted.
install.sh: exact entry-set check, rejection of non-regular entries, private extraction directory, symlink-refusing destination directories, staged replace, and pre-mktemp trap.
build-release.py: source SHA-256 is verified before extraction, the archive is rejected on absolute, '..', link or special members, and the SDK is always rebuilt from the authenticated tarball.

dependency-licenses.py requires --openssl-source for bundled builds and appends the OpenSSL and Text::Template notices. The openssl-src branch is dead because the bundled-openssl feature adds no dependency; this is harmless.
Workflows are dispatch-only, use pinned action SHAs and persist-credentials:false, and the self-hosted job refuses ZEROPW_* environment.
limitations: Static review only. Nothing was built, run or installed. File SHA-256 values were not checked against the head.

Supplied execution evidence references 06869b6 (focused tests) and e3d240e (SDK build), not 01ef0ca. Tooling tests were 'being rerun'. Full macOS and Linux matrices, archive installation, and final-source Homebrew are pending.

StateDir::lock, write_bytes and append_line were not supplied. The serialization claims for N1, N3 and N4 assume the lock is re-entrant within a thread, exclusive across threads and processes, and that write_bytes is atomic.
Transport, vault and CLI secret-write callers, incident.rs and smtp.rs were not supplied. It was not checked that every production shared-secret write goes through membership::author_commit.
openssl-sys environment-precedence behavior in NEW-2 is based on the crate's documented lookup order, not observed in this repository's build.
This is a scoped review of the supplied files and is not repository or release acceptance. No earlier PASS carries over.
